LESSON: READING 1.2.1 PRE- READING LETTER - SOUND KNOWLEDGE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Greetings Suggested vocabulary Good morning, good afternoon, hello, good evening
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Pre- reading Letter - sound Knowledge
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 1.2.1 Pre- reading Letter - sound Knowledge, part of Greetings Suggested vocabulary Good morning, good afternoon, hello, good evening in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: How do we sit while reading? 2. How do we position our books while reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Pre- reading Letter - sound Knowledge together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: learner’s ability to speak clearly and effectively is enhanced as they use appropriate language structure (verb ‘to

be’) to describe himself/herself, and other people.

• Learning to learn: learner’s ability to acquire self-discipline is enhanced as they are motivated and practise introducing oneself and others

using the verb ‘to be’.

Values:
Responsibility: is developed as learners take care of reading materials entrusted to them.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life Skills(Self-awareness): The learner’s self-awareness is enhanced as the learner identifies the appropriate posture for reading preparedness.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Kiswahili Language Activities as learners sit in the appropriate posture when reading.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Flash cards/charts, videos, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted

digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
